question.problem:
| $x$ | $0$ | $2$ | $4$ | $8$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $0.1$ | $0.7$ | $0.1$ | $0.1$ |

Let ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{101}$ be a random sample of size $n=101$ from a population with the probability mass function given above. Find an approximation for the probability that the sample mean is between $2.5$ and $3.$

*Note: $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*
question.worked_solution:
Suppose that ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population standard deviation $\sigma .$ The central limit theorem (or CLT) states that for sufficiently large $n,$ the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ can be approximated as 

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

In our case:

- the sample size is 

$$
n=101,
$$

- the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\text{E}[X] \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}f({x}_{i}) \\  & =0\cdot 0.1+2\cdot 0.7+4\cdot 0.1+8\cdot 0.1 \\  & =0+1.4+0.4+0.8 \\  & =2.6,\end{aligned}
$$

- the population variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\text{Var}[X] \\  & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =({0}^{2}\cdot 0.1+{2}^{2}\cdot 0.7+{4}^{2}\cdot 0.1+{8}^{2}\cdot 0.1)-{2.6}^{2} \\  & =(0+2.8+1.6+6.4)-6.76 \\  & =4.04.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by the CLT, we have that the distribution of the sample mean can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}) \\  & ∼N\,(2.6,\frac{4.04}{101}) \\  & ∼N(2.6,0.04).\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find $P(2.5<\overset{―}{X}<3).$ So, we convert $\overset{―}{X}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(2.5<\overset{―}{X}<3) & ≈P(\frac{2.5-2.6}{\sqrt{0.04}}<Z<\frac{3-2.6}{\sqrt{0.04}}) \\  & =P(-0.5<Z<2) \\  & =Φ(2)-Φ(-0.5).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
P(2.5<\overset{―}{X}<3)=Φ(2)-Φ(-0.5).
$$
